# Data Dictionary

## Canonical feature list

The single source of truth for every engineered feature is
**`outputs/feature_analysis/feature_registry.csv`**, generated by
`scripts/build_modeling_dataset.py` directly from each feature module's `describe_features()`
function (co-located with the feature-building code, so it cannot silently drift out of sync).
It contains, per feature: `feature_name`, `description`, `source_table`, `source_season`
(`t` or `t-1`, see `docs/data_leakage_rules.md`), `transformation`, `known_before_kickoff`,
`missing_value_treatment`, `expected_direction`, `category`.

This document does not re-enumerate all ~133 features — see the registry for that. Below is
the raw-table glossary (the source data every feature is built from) and the modeling table's
non-feature columns.

## Modeling table identity/target columns

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `school` | Canonical team identifier (matches `teams.school`, the natural key every source table joins on) |
| `season` | Target season `t` |
| `regular_season_wins` | Games won where `school` was FBS, `season_type='regular'` (see limitation #2 in `docs/assumptions_and_limitations.md` re: conference championship games) |
| `regular_season_losses` | Games lost, same scope |
| `scheduled_games` | Total games played, same scope |

## Raw source tables (`SQL Scripts/schema.sql`)

| Table | Grain | Season coverage | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `teams` | one row per school | n/a | canonical join key everywhere |
| `games` | one row per game | 2013–2025 | `targets.py`, `schedule.py`, `program_history.py` |
| `betting_lines` | one row per (game, provider) | 2013–2025 | not used (evaluated and rejected as a preseason signal — see assumptions doc) |
| `team_talent` | one row per (season, school) | 2015–2025 | `talent_recruiting.py` |
| `coaches` | one row per (coach, school, season) | 2004–2025 | `coaching.py`, `program_history.py` |
| `team_rosters` | one row per (athlete, season) | 2004–2025 | `roster_turnover.py`, `talent_recruiting.py`, `program_history.py` |
| `recruiting_players` | one row per (recruit, class year) | recruit_year 2000–2025 | `talent_recruiting.py`, `roster_turnover.py` |
| `returning_production` | one row per (season, team) | 2014–2025 | `returning_production.py` |
| `game_team_stats` | one row per (game, team) | 2013–2025 | `prior_performance.py`, `program_history.py` |
| `plays` | one row per play | 2013–2025 | `prior_performance.py`, `program_history.py` |

See `SQL Scripts/README.md` and `SQL Scripts/schema.sql` for exact column lists, types, and
known raw-data quirks (compound "X-Y" string fields, generated numeric columns, etc.) — this
project's Python code queries those tables directly rather than re-deriving a separate copy of
that documentation here.

## Feature categories (see feature_registry.csv `category` column)

`prior_performance`, `returning_production`, `talent_recruiting`, `roster_turnover`,
`coaching`, `schedule`, `program_history` — one Python module per category under
`src/cfb_win_total_model/features/`.
